The Story of King Vinayadhar

I bow to Lord Jina, who illuminates all things in the entire world through pure omniscience, and I write the story of King Vinayadhar, who possessed the virtue of faith — a story dear to the noble.

Vinayadhar was king of Hastinapur, the capital of the Kurujangal region. His queen was Vinayavati. In that city lived a merchant named Vrushabsen, whose wife was Vrushabsena. They had an intelligent son named Jindas.

Vinayadhar was deeply lustful. Once, he contracted a terrible disease. Truly, excessive indulgence in sensual pleasure beyond proper limits becomes the cause of suffering. The king had many great physicians treat him, but his disease could not be cured in any way. The king was greatly distressed by this illness. He found no peace day or night.

The king had a minister named Siddharth, who was a Jain and possessed pure right faith. One day, this minister brought the water used to wash the feet of a monk endowed with the power of healing through foot-washing — water that destroys all diseases — and gave it to the king. The king, a true devotee of Lord Jina, drank that water with great faith. Upon drinking it, all his disease vanished, just as darkness disappears when the sun rises.

Truly, who can describe the power of the austerities of the noble, through whose very foot-washing water all diseases are pacified? Just as Minister Siddharth gave the pure water of dharma to the king, so too should other worthy souls give the water of dharma to all, pacifying the heat of worldly suffering.

May the monk, the supreme scholar of Jain philosophy, the holder of the power of healing through foot-washing, grant me peace and happiness.

The faith shown in Jain dharma — in the pure acts of charity, worship, vows, and fasting done according to Jain dharma — destroys suffering. The incidental fruit of this faith is the attainment of the wealth of Indra, Chakravartin, Vidyadhar, and others. And the real fruit is omniscience, in which the soul's special powers of infinite knowledge, infinite vision, infinite bliss, and infinite energy manifest. May that faith bring welfare to you, O worthy souls.

This story teaches that faith in the pure dharma and in the power of saints can bring miraculous healing and welfare. King Vinayadhar's disease, which no physician could cure, was destroyed simply by drinking the foot-washing water of a monk, taken with faith. The wise should cultivate faith in the true dharma and in those who practise it with sincerity, for such faith is the destroyer of all suffering.
